# Results — Study 244 (Asset-Growth) on the real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: total-asset YoY
growth rate (AG) from annual 10-K filings (Assets concept) via the shared EDGAR cache.
Returns from `_edgar_yrret.parquet` (Yahoo Finance). As-of **2026-06-16**.*

**Definition**:
- AG_t = (Total_Assets_t − Total_Assets_{t-1}) / Total_Assets_{t-1}

**Reporting lag**: fundamentals from fiscal year y → returns in calendar year y+1.
**Universe**: current S&P 500 members with Assets present (~370 tickers/year average).
**Window**: 17 years of signal (2009–2025), forecasting returns 2010–2026.

**SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the EDGAR panel covers only current S&P 500 members
projected backwards. Every firm in the panel survived to 2026. All results are upper
bounds on a live strategy — the true live effect is unknown.

## Verdict

The predicted effect (high asset growth → low returns) is **absent** on this panel. The
long-low-AG/short-high-AG hedge yields only **−1.0%/yr** with HAC *t* = **−0.45** —
statistically indistinguishable from zero and in the *wrong direction*. High-AG firms
(fast growers) actually earn a marginally higher raw return (+20.9%/yr) than low-AG
firms (+19.9%/yr) on this survivor panel. The direction is inverted relative to the
academic claim.

The academic effect (Cooper, Gulen & Schill 2008) was documented on an all-US-stocks
universe with thousands of names including small and mid-caps. On a survivorship-biased
S&P 500 large-cap panel, fast-growing large caps that survived include successful
technology and growth companies (FAANG-type names) that powered the 2010s bull market.
Firms that grew assets aggressively and subsequently failed are simply absent from the
panel.

- **Signal — NONE** (hedge t = −0.45, wrong direction; no evidence of the predicted
  effect on this panel; literature supports effect for broader non-biased universe
  of small/mid-caps, not for survivor large-caps).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (no signal to trade; long-short L/S inverts direction on
  this panel; even if the academic effect is real in its original universe, it does
  not appear here).
